newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dirt begins to fly again between Kremlin insiders.
newsitem.headline: Dirt begins to fly again between Kremlin insiders.

text.p: A fragile political truce between past and present Kremlin insiders broke down on Friday, opening the way for fresh infighting between President Boris Yeltsin's current and former staffs.

The longtime feud between Anatoly Chubais, the president's chief of staff, and his former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov, appeared to have resumed in earnest, less than two weeks after Yeltsin himself underwent heart surgery.

A Moscow newspaper printed the transcript of what it said was a bugged conversation between Chubais and two other Yeltsin aides on June 22. This was two days after Korzhakov was sacked by Yeltsin at the insistence of Chubais, who at the time was coordinating the president's re-election campaign.

Chubais denied the authenticity of the tape, published in Moskovsky Komsomolets which hinted broadly that it came from quarters close to Korzhakov, who until his dismissal headed the presidential security service.

The transcript shows Chubais and top Yeltsin aide Viktor Ilyushin conspiring to block an investigation by prosecutors into the detention by Korzhakov's security men of two of their campaign staff with half a million dollars in cash.

At the time all those involved in the incident, which took place between rounds one and two of the presidential election, denied that the two men were carrying the money and insisted they were framed.

In the transcript Ilyushin telephones Russia's prosecutor-general Yuri Skuratov and tells him not to pass on the file on the case to investigators until after the second round of the election so the facts should not leak out.
Chubais, according to the transcript, orders that Korzhakov should be told to keep his mouth shut or "I will put him in jail".
Chubais says in the transcript he has enough documented dirt about Korzhakov's "thieving, murders and bloodshed" to put him behind bars for 15 years.
Moskovsky Komsomolets, the Russian capital's most popular daily, said it had no doubts about the authenticity of the recording, though parts of it were inaudible.

Yeltsin aide Sergei Krasavchenko, named as the third participant, denied that any such meeting had taken place. But parliament's lower house, the Duma, which is packed with Chubais's enemies, said it would investigate the affair.

Korzhakov launched a political career of his own this week, officially nominating himself as a candidate for a by-election in Tula next February. The seat was formerly held by Alexander Lebed, also sacked by Yeltsin in October after four stormy months as the president's national security adviser.
Registration as a parliamentary candidate gives Korzhakov temporary immunity from arrest and prosecution. If he wins the seat, he will continue to enjoy immunity.
A racy Moscow weekly, Sovershenno Sekretno, published a long interview with Korzhakov on Friday in which he expressed fears he might be arrested on Chubais's orders.
The interview was originally recorded some weeks ago for television. But the magazine said all of Russia's main channels, which are under direct or indirect Kremlin influence, refused to screen it.

Korzhakov boasted in the interview that Chubais and his allies "are very afraid of me" and repeated allegations that the president's chief of staff was effectively running the country as a regent with the aid of Yeltsin's daughter Tatyana.
The burly former KGB bodyguard was a close friend of the Yeltsin family until his sacking. He is now at odds with Yeltsin and has formed a political partnership with Lebed.
